_comment: Identifies this project's PRODUCT: the discriminant every neoize graph node carries, so one Neo4j server holds many products plus the universal `shared` layer without them colliding. In global mode a session reads the UNION of `shared` and this product; it writes structure and project lessons to this product; genuinely universal lessons are promoted up to `shared` with `neoize promote`. A project-mode graph is self-contained and has no shared layer. A product can span several repos; give each repo's .neoize/project.json the same product id and they contribute to one graph. `mode` is the server lifecycle: `global` (recommended) uses the one shared server at ~/.neoize alongside every other product; `project` runs this project's own container. Copy to .neoize/project.json, set the id (lowercase, stable) and version-control it. `neoize product --set <id> --mode global` writes it for you. If this file is absent the product defaults to the git repo name and the mode to global. Optional `symbols_refresh` is a shell command `neoize apply` runs to regenerate and load this project's symbol layer (its language-specific extractor and loader, which the plugin cannot do generically); it runs with NEOIZE_PRODUCT and NEOIZE_NEO4J_CONTAINER bound and keyed to this product. Omit it if the project has no symbol layer.
